content:
This topic follows the naming from #38039 which implements the discussed naming scheme from #mathlib4 > naming convention: `UniformSpace.Completion` morphisms.

In #40151, we had a discussion about whether to use [IsUniformAddGroup F]or (hf : UniformContinuous f) as assumptions for the new ContinuousLinearMap.fromCompletion. The former was chosen because that was consistent with the other .fromCompletion(prior to #38039 called .extension) maps. However, the theorem ContinuousLinearMap.UniformContinuous shows that the latter is the weaker assumption. Since in general we want to have the most general statements in the library, should we update the .fromCompletion maps to use this weaker assumption? Or is there a reason not to do this?

Since in general we want to have the most general statements in the library

I think maximum generality is usually fine, unless it causes more pain than gain.

And in this case, I think there is very little gain (what spaces satisfy everything except IsUniformAddGroup?), and more pain (needing to have a proof for UniformContinuous f, which in the IsUniformAddGroup case it's just f.uniformContinuous, but still a pain to write over-and-over).

If an example comes up where someone actually needs that kind of generality, then sure.
You could also use an autoparam to encode the discharging of the proof obligation so that users don't have to, in the common "trivial" case
